title: Polynomial-time equality of unary values
statement: Let $f,g$ be functions from bit strings to natural numbers, and suppose that the unary encodings of both functions' values are polynomial-time computable. Then the Boolean-valued function returning true exactly when $f(x)=g(x)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: the unary encoding of f is polynomial-time computable
the unary encoding of g is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If two unary values are polynomial-time computable, then the single-bit test deciding their equality is polynomial-time computable, as the conjunction of the two unary comparisons.
